title: A Constructive Relationship and Capstone Workshop
summary: Brings the programme together around building trust with the authority, followed by a workshop in which participants assess a case-study firm as a supervisor would and plan its engagement.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together around building trust with the authority, followed by a workshop in which participants assess a case-study firm as a supervisor would and plan its engagement.
Learning Objectives: Design an engagement strategy built on openness and no surprises
Apply the supervisor's method to assess a firm end to end
Produce an action plan to strengthen the firm's supervisory relationship
Syllabus: Openness, notifications and the cost of surprises
Relationship mapping, regulatory liaison and board reporting on supervision
Common misunderstandings between firms and supervisors
Workshop: assessing a case-study firm and planning its supervisory engagement
Intended Audience: Chief executives, senior managers and executive directors who meet the supervisor
Heads of compliance, risk, finance and internal audit and their teams who prepare the firm for supervision
Company secretaries, regulatory liaison and relationship managers who coordinate supervisory engagement
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of senior management, compliance, risk or finance work in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of working for an authority is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
